newsitem.title: INDIA: India monsoon rains may hit soybean region Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: India monsoon rains may hit soybean region Tuesday.

text.p: Southwest monsoon rains, which arrived in India nine days late, are likely to hit the central state of Madhya Pradesh on Tuesday, a senior Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) official said.
"Monsoon rains are likely to hit Madhya Pradesh tomorrow," A.V.R. Krishna Rao told Reuters on Monday.
Madhya Pradesh produces about 80 percent of the country's soybean output.
Rao said monsoon rains had fully covered the southern states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka and most of Andhra Pradesh.
"They have also covered most northeastern states," Rao said.
He said monsoon rains hit parts of the western states of Maharashtra and Gujarat on Monday. Maharashtra is India's main cotton-growing region and Gujarat produces the bulk of India's groundnut crop.
"Monsoon rains arrived in Bombay today," Rao said.
He said the IMD might provide an update on the impact of El Nino warm water currents on India's monsoon rains within the next three days.

Oil World reported last week that the development of El Nino in the southern Pacific had increased the chances of drought across southeast Asia, Australia and India, threatening oilseeds and grain crops.
El Nino raises the water temperature off the coast of South America and can disrupt weather patterns worldwide.

Meteorological officials last week said it was too early to determine how El Nino would affect India's annual southwestern monsoon rains. They had said the department would provide an update on El Nino's impact later this month.
The IMD has forecast a 10th successive normal monsoon in 1997. --Sambit Mohanty, New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
